subject: Staging reclaim deep runtime validation (incl. 16 KB, stress)
scope: Deep runtime validation of the committed staging-reclamation patch (tools/vulkan-wrapper/staging-reclaim.patch) beyond the first A/B pass. Two emulator phases were run on exclusive port 5556: Phase 1 AVD Vapor_UI_API36 (4 KB pages) and Phase 2 AVD Vapor_API_37_16KB (16 KB pages). Cases: unfenced one-time submit, begin/reset reclamation in isolation, vkQueueSubmit2 and semaphore submissions, 32-image and long-lived-image stress with peak-tracked accounting and RSS, 16 KB A/B, and an attempted Khronos validation-layer run. A new scratch-only probe fixture (probe-deep.c) drove the extra cases; no repo file other than this receipt was created or modified and nothing was committed.

phase2.fixture_note: The first Phase 2 run batch crashed with `Segmentation fault` (exit 139) for all 5 runs because the probe-deep binary then in use was linked with 4 KB LOAD alignment (0x1000) and cannot run on the 16 KB-page guest. The probe was rebuilt with -Wl,-z,max-page-size=16384 -Wl,-z,common-page-size=16384 (LOAD 0x4000) and the same 5 runs were repeated successfully once. The failed-attempt exit codes remain in <workspace>/staging-deep/runs.tsv; that was a fixture error, not a wrapper defect.

protocol.command_template: adb -s emulator-5556 shell "cd /data/local/tmp/vapor-staging-deep && LD_LIBRARY_PATH=. PREFIX=. WRAPPER_LOG_LEVEL=debug WRAPPER_CMD_LOG_LEVEL=none FORCE_BCN_EMULATION=1 USE_IMAGE_VIEW=<0|1> ./probe-deep ./<patched-stripped.so|candidate.so> <MODE> <PARAM> 16"

probe_modes.staging: base probe behaviour: non-one-time command buffer per cycle, fence submit/wait, free per cycle (4 KB anchor)
probe_modes.oneshot: ONE_TIME_SUBMIT command buffer + classic vkQueueSubmit with fence, wait, free
probe_modes.nofence: ONE_TIME_SUBMIT command buffer submitted with VK_NULL_HANDLE fence, vkDeviceWaitIdle for completion, then free
probe_modes.reset-cb: one re-submittable command buffer reused across cycles; release point under test is vkResetCommandBuffer
probe_modes.reset-pool-begin: one command buffer; vkResetCommandPool (not hooked by the patch) then vkBeginCommandBuffer is the release point
probe_modes.free-norebegin: re-submittable command buffer freed without reset/re-begin (release expected in vkFreeCommandBuffers)
probe_modes.semaphore: ONE_TIME_SUBMIT submitted with a binary signal semaphore and NO fence; a second valid submission waits that semaphore with a fence
probe_modes.stress-images: 32 images x 8 CmdCopyBufferToImage copies, one submitted command buffer per image, RSS sampled
probe_modes.stress-long: one long-lived image x 256 copies, one command buffer per copy, RSS sampled

protocol.log_analysis: <workspace>/staging-deep/summary-runs.json (sha256 eb82be981754714e3a7b91504418e7c12ccaaf65428d5c75c2a1c89f7fa82e66) computes tracking, release calls/totals, peak tracked resources, marker intervals and tracked==released from the raw debug logs.

results.summary: 23 successful runs: 18 in Phase 1 (4 KB) and 5 in Phase 2 (16 KB), all exit code 0, 'PASS clean-exit', no FAIL lines, no wrapper staging-path errors, no probe crashes/tombstones. tracking==released and peak-tracked accounting hold in every patched and control run. 5 additional Phase 2 attempts exited 139 because of the 4 KB-aligned probe binary and were repeated after rebuilding the probe (fixture error, see emulator.phase2.fixture_note).

anchor_4kb_ab.verdict: PASS. Patched: 32 tracking events, 64 resources released in 32 two-resource calls inside vkFreeCommandBuffers, peak 2 tracked. Control: 32 tracking events, 64 resources released in one call at vkDestroyImage, peak 64 tracked. Both tracking==released.

case1_unfenced_one_time.verdict: PASS. 8 ONE_TIME_SUBMIT command buffers submitted without a fence: no release at vkDeviceWaitIdle (resources are unstamped, as designed), all 16 resources released inside vkFreeCommandBuffers; no leak (tracking==released), no crash. Control releases 16 at image destroy.

reset_command_buffer.verdict: PASS. All 8 two-resource releases occur between MARKER before-reset-cb and MARKER after-reset-cb (inside vkResetCommandBuffer); nothing is released before that point. Control keeps 16 resources until image destroy.

reset_pool_then_begin.verdict: PASS. vkResetCommandPool is not hooked by the patch, so no release happens there; the subsequent vkBeginCommandBuffer releases the previous cycle's resources (7 of 8 releases between before-begin/after-begin; the final command buffer's resources are released when it is freed after the loop, hence one extra before-free/after-free interval). Control keeps 16 resources until image destroy.

free_without_rebegin.verdict: PASS. Re-submittable command buffers freed without any reset/re-begin release their staging resources inside vkFreeCommandBuffers (8 x 2 = 16); tracking==released.

queue_submit2.verdict: PASS. The patched WRAPPER_QueueSubmit2 path stamps the submission fence: all 8 two-resource releases occur inside vkWaitForFences (between before-wait/after-wait), proving the QueueSubmit2 reclaim path works at runtime. Control keeps 16 resources until image destroy.

binary_semaphore_without_fence.verdict: PASS (no crash) but documents the patch's known limitation: semaphore-only completion is not tracked. The one-time command buffer's resources are not stamped (no fence passed to vkQueueSubmit), so no early release happens at the semaphore/fence wait of the second submission; all 16 resources are released inside vkFreeCommandBuffers. tracking==released, no leak past command-buffer destruction.

images_32x8.verdict: PASS. 256 copies (32 images x 8) = 512 tracked resources. Patched peak 16 tracked (one image's 8 copies x 2 while its command buffer is alive), released 512 in 32 calls; control peak 512 (all live until image destroy), released 512 in 32 calls at destroy. tracking==released in both. RSS: see raw lines in summary-runs.json.

long_lived_1x256.verdict: PASS. 256 copies into one long-lived image = 512 tracked resources. Patched peak 2 tracked (one copy x 2), released 512 across 256 calls; control peak 512 with a single 512-resource release at image destroy. tracking==released in both.

case4_stress_growth.rss_observation: RSS was sampled from /proc/self/status inside the probe (process-start, after-setup, mid-upload at copy 128, after-upload, after-image-destroy, before/after-device-destroy). It stayed in the 21-25 MB range and did not separate patched from control at this scale; the tracked-resource peaks (2/16 vs 64/512) are the meaningful signal, not RSS on a software driver with caching allocators.

staging_32_cycles.verdict: PASS. page_size=16384; patched releases 64 resources in 32 two-resource calls inside vkFreeCommandBuffers (peak 2) vs control one 64-resource release at vkDestroyImage (peak 64); tracking==released both.

case6_validation_layer.verdict: NOT RUN / NOT FEASIBLE with this probe architecture; no VUID claim is made.
attempts: Downloaded the official Khronos asset android-binaries-1.4.363.0.tar.gz (libVkLayer_khronos_validation.so for arm64-v8a present); scratch file <workspace>/staging-deep/vvl-android.tar.gz sha256 b2727789f4c4d83b7149e904768bbaf54e8236ec912691730a70e22aebcba419. It was not installed because the probe never goes through the Vulkan loader.

The extended probe (like the repo probe) dlopens the wrapper directly as an ICD and uses vk_icdGetInstanceProcAddr, bypassing the Vulkan loader; Khronos validation layers are loader layers and cannot be attached to this path.

Loader-path attempt 1: dlopen /system/lib64/libvulkan.so with VK_ICD_FILENAMES=<patched.so> -> the device enumerated and ran but produced no wrapper debug output and the BC1 pixel check failed (rgba 0,248,0,0), i.e. the native ranchu/lavapipe ICD was used instead of the wrapper. Logs: p1-loader-smoke.log.

Loader-path attempt 2: VK_LOADER_DEBUG=error,warn,info plus a valid wrapper ICD manifest JSON -> VK_LOADER_DEBUG and the ICD selection still had no effect (no loader/layer diagnostics in the guest output; same uncompressed-BC1 pixel failure). Logs: p1-loader-debug.log, p1-loader-json.log.

No /vendor/etc/vulkan/icd.d or /system/etc/vulkan/icd.d config was writable/visible from the shell on this image, and modifying system partitions was out of scope; therefore the validation layer could not be attached to the patched wrapper without a different loader-based fixture.

control_comparison_summary: In every case where the unpatched candidate.so was run (same probe, same environment), it retained all tracked staging resources until image/device destroy and released them in a single call there; the patched library always released them at the completion-gated point under test, with the same totals and tracking==released.
defects_found: None. The patch behaved as designed in all executed cases. Non-defect observations: (1) semaphore-only completion does not trigger early reclaim (documented design limitation of the patch, no leak past command-buffer destruction); (2) RSS is not a discriminating metric on this software driver; (3) the first 16 KB batch failed only because the scratch probe was 4 KB-aligned - fixed by rebuilding the probe, not by changing the wrapper.
confirmed: Patch identity: tools/vulkan-wrapper/staging-reclaim.patch sha256 c92b69ebbbf244c74d05455e1bfff3da0c0aaff94bbd8a75ab4dc4f6308a6568 in repo at HEAD 95ecbf62; device library is the stripped form of the recorded scratch build (lib sha256 e8eae86b..., stripped 08ef8247...).
Case 1 (unfenced one-time submit) PASS: resources released at vkFreeCommandBuffers, not at vkDeviceWaitIdle, tracking==released, no crash.

Case 2 (begin/reset in isolation) PASS: vkResetCommandBuffer and vkBeginCommandBuffer each release the previous recording's staging resources at that call (release log between the probe's markers), and free-without-rebegin releases at vkFreeCommandBuffers.

Case 3 PASS for vkQueueSubmit2+fence (release inside vkWaitForFences) and PASS-with-documented-limitation for binary-semaphore-only completion (no early release; released at command-buffer free; no crash/no leak).

Case 4 PASS: 32 images x 8 copies peak 16 tracked vs control 512; one long-lived image x 256 copies peak 2 vs control 512; both released 512 total; tracking==released; RSS recorded but not discriminating.

Case 5 PASS on the real 16 KB guest (PAGE_SIZE and probe sysconf both 16384): 32-cycle staging A/B, 32-cycle one-time+fence A/B, and 8-cycle image-view one-time+fence run all release at the expected points, tracking==released, no crashes.
No wrapper staging-path errors, no probe crashes or tombstones in any successful run; only the known benign wrapper banner appears once per debug log.
Control (candidate.so, unpatched) behaves as the previous review described in every A/B: single release of all tracked resources at image destroy.
still_pending: No physical phone/GPU run: all runtime evidence is llvmpipe/Goldfish GFXStream software Vulkan on emulators; the patch's behavior on a production Adreno/Mali driver is unverified.

The wrapper-emulated-memory path (VK_EXT_map_memory_placed + VkPhysicalDeviceMapMemoryPlacedFeaturesEXT.memoryMapPlaced) was still not testable on llvmpipe, so the raw-dispatch staging allocation change and the O1 double-free fix are not runtime-proven.
Khronos validation layers could not be attached (probe bypasses the Vulkan loader; loader path does not load the wrapper on this image); no VUID cleanliness is claimed.
Concurrency/thread-safety stress was not run; the wrapper still relies on Vulkan external synchronization.
No real game/streaming workload or long-duration memory measurement; the peak-tracked counts are from a synthetic probe, not from a game.
Timeline semaphores are not tracked by the patch; only binary-semaphore submissions were exercised (and they document the limitation).
No performance/FPS measurement; timings are not collected because WRAPPER_LOG_LEVEL=debug dominates the run time.
16 KB evidence covers A/B staging and one-time+fence only; stress cases were not repeated on the 16 KB guest.
limitations: Software Vulkan (llvmpipe) on both phases; no hardware driver behavior.
Probe uses synthetic BC1 data and its own offscreen copy path; no game assets, no Steam/Wine/window.
Single graphics/compute queue, single-threaded host, synchronous fence waits.
The extended probe is a new scratch-only fixture; it does not replace the repo probe for the existing protocol, and its staging/copy logic mirrors tools/tests/vulkan-wrapper-native.c.
RSS from /proc/self/status is not a reliable allocation measure on this driver; peaks of tracked wrapper resources were derived from the wrapper's own debug log lines.
